Header: Ceratitis capitata and Bactrocera dorsalis (previously B. invadens )

Prevention: Pick and destroy all fallen and cracked fruits on the ground and from the tree and bury them throughout the season.
Dig the ground below the tree canopy to expose the insect (maggot and pupa) to sunlight and predators.
Farmers must not mix late maturing varieties (e.g.
Apple mango) in the same field because late varieties are attacked by the population that builds up during the ripening of early varieties
It is important to manage insect pests in alternative hosts such as guava, citrus, cherimoya and papaya near the mango field.
Monitoring: Hot weather conditions are favourable for fruit fly development.
Inspect the soil underneath the mango tree once a week from
Look for maggots and reddish brown pupa that is of the same size as a grain of wheat.
Look for reddish puncture marks on the fruit surface that progress with a yellow margin with time, from
Look for white maggots in the fruit flesh.
Affected parts show a black soft rot on the fruit surface.
Be ready to control pests when 1 in 50 fruits is infested with the maggots.
Direct Control: Remove all infested fruits from the tree and ground.
Throughout the season, collect all infested fruits and bury them 50cm below ground. (Note that this management option will only help your crop the following season and not the current season.)
Restrictions: Avoid drinking, eating and smoking while handling and applying pesticides.
Spray in the evening or early in the morning and observe a pre-harvest interval of 2 weeks.
Spray the entire tree every 2 weeks with cypermethrin (e.g
Rocket,) at 1ml per 1L of water from
July onwards until 2 weeks before harvest.
